outcome: Duration of second stage of labor
Local anesthetic use (mg bupivacaine equivalents per hour)
cohort: The participants were 938 healthy parturients (465 accepted continuous epidural infusion and 473 accepted intermittent epidural bolus for labor analgesia) from 11 randomized controlled trials.
finding: Intermittent epidural bolus (IEB) demonstrated greater benefits over continuous epidural infusion (CEI) by slightly reducing local anesthetic use, lowering the risk of instrumental delivery, and improving maternal satisfaction during labor analgesia.
mod_finding: There was no statistical difference in the cesarean delivery rate between IEB and CEI, but IEB was associated with a statistically significant lessened risk of instrumental delivery.
